related_questions.question: Is it possible to have COVID and test negative?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, it is possible to have COVID-19 and test negative, particularly with antigen tests. Antigen tests are less sensitive than molecular tests (like PCR tests) and may not detect the virus, especially in the early stages of infection or if symptoms are mild. If a test is negative but symptoms persist, it's recommended to consider other possible illnesses, such as influenza or RSV, and potentially retest with a molecular test or seek medical advice.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, it is possible to have COVID-19 and test negative, particularly with antigen tests

list.title: Sensitivity of Antigen Tests:
list.snippet: Antigen tests detect viral proteins, while molecular tests (PCR) detect viral genetic material. Antigen tests are faster and more convenient but are less sensitive, meaning they may not detect the virus if the viral load is low.

list.title: Timing of Testing:
list.snippet: The timing of the test in relation to symptom onset is crucial. Early in infection, the viral load may be too low for an antigen test to detect, even if the person is infected.

list.title: Other Respiratory Illnesses:
list.snippet: Other respiratory viruses, like influenza and RSV, can cause similar symptoms to COVID-19. A negative COVID-19 test doesn't rule out these other illnesses.

list.title: Recommendations:
list.snippet: The CDC recommends repeat testing with antigen tests or using molecular tests if symptoms persist despite a negative antigen test, according to the CDC.
